sections.body: Puberty is driven by hormones (mainly oestrogen and testosterone). These cause growth, body changes and the ability to reproduce.
Human reproduction: a sperm cell from a male joins an egg cell from a female (fertilisation). The fertilised egg can grow into a baby in the uterus over about 9 months.
The menstrual cycle (periods) is about monthly and is a normal sign that the body is preparing for possible pregnancy.
Healthy relationships of any kind are built on respect, trust, honesty and consent. Nobody should pressure you to do anything you're not ready for.
Questions are normal. Trusted adults, school nurses, doctors and reliable health websites can help.

options: When a sperm cell joins an egg cell
hints: It's the very first step of reproduction.
Plants are fertilised when pollen reaches the ovule. In humans, which cells join?
quiz.explain: Fertilisation is when a sperm cell and an egg cell join.

quiz.q: What are healthy relationships built on?
options: Doing whatever the other person says
hints: Think about how good friends treat each other.
A good friendship has trust and respect. Romantic relationships need the same and more.
quiz.explain: Healthy relationships are based on respect, trust, honesty and consent.

quiz.q: Which hormones mainly drive the changes of puberty?
hints: Hormones are chemical messengers. The lesson names two main ones for puberty.
Think of the sex hormones: one is made mainly in the ovaries, the other mainly in the testes.
Insulin is the hormone that controls blood sugar; it's made in the pancreas. Each hormone has its own job.
quiz.explain: Oestrogen and testosterone are the main hormones behind puberty's growth and body changes. Adrenaline, insulin, melatonin and serotonin are real chemical messengers with other jobs.
